subject: DPA: Security Annex & Subprocessor Flow — counsel comments
messages:
From: Amir Khan <amir.khan@novahealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Stone <r.stone@novahealth.com>, PrivacyCounsel <privacy@lexbridge.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: NovaHealth DPA redlines + security annex questions

Marcus —

Attached are NovaHealth's first-pass DPA redlines (PDF) and a short security annex our vendor-risk team asked us to include. High level items:

- We need clarification on your subprocessors (list + effective dates) and whether any subprocessors process EEA data.
- Data transfer mechanism: vendor-risk prefers an EU-hosted instance or SCCs with mandatory audit rights; counsel flagged your standard EU-US addendum as light on audit wording.
- Audit / compliance evidence: can you provide SOC 2 Type II (most recent) and pen test summary under NDA?
- Retention / deletion: we redlined a 90-day deletion window for non-transactional logs — can you confirm feasibility?

We prefer AdobeSign for execution. Please confirm receipt and propose next steps.

Attachments: NovaHealth_DPA_Redline_v1.pdf, Security_Annex_draft.docx

Thanks,
Amir
Amir Khan
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Vendor Risk
NovaHealth

Subject: Re: NovaHealth DPA redlines + security annex questions

Amir —

Thanks for the redlines and the annex. Confirm received. High-level response and next steps below: 

1) Subprocessors: we'll provide an up-to-date subprocessor registry (CSV) with effective dates by EOD tomorrow. Key subprocessors that may touch EEA data are: VectorCompute (inference hosting), CacheLayer Inc. (KV cache), and LogsFlow (aggregated telemetry). We'll flag EU-only instances where applicable.

2) Data transfers: Redwood supports SCCs (model: standard EU SCCs) and can add the EU-US addendum language you're asking for. We can also discuss a dedicated EU-hosted deployment under Redwood Dedicated if NovaHealth requires physical residency — timeline & pricing differ.

3) Audit evidence: we can provide SOC 2 Type II report and redacted pen test report under NDA. Will route SOC2 via secure share (we'll need an executed NDA).

4) Retention: 90-day deletion for non-transactional logs is plausible; need to confirm specifics (which logs you consider "non-transactional"). We typically retain aggregated telemetry 90 days and request-level logs 365 days by default for debugging. If you need shorter windows we can add controls or masking rules.

5) Execution: AdobeSign is fine. We typically run DocuSign, but can use AdobeSign — procurement note about signatory email addresses and contact for SOW/PO.

Proposed next steps:
- I will upload subprocessor CSV + SOC2 redacted report (NDA required).
- Neha (cc'd) will draft alternate proposal language for the EU transfer clause and a short audit clause amendment.
- Let's schedule a 30-min call with your vendor-risk team tomorrow afternoon to walk redlines.

I can loop in our solutions engineer if you want to scope a Dedicated/EU-hosted option.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | (415) 555-0124

Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 11:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NovaHealth DPA redlines + security annex questions

Amir / Marcus —

I've reviewed the redlines and vendor-risk asks. A few privacy-counsel level notes and suggested language to keep the commercial rhythm while addressing NovaHealth's risk team concerns: 

- EU Transfers: propose this compromise: Redwood will (a) execute the standard SCCs and (b) add an explicit audit-window clause: "Customer or an independent auditor (under NDA) may audit Processor's relevant controls with 30 days' notice and subject to agreed scoping to minimize production impact." We prefer limiting frequency to once per 12 months unless material incident.

- Subprocessors: we'll provide a CSV and implement an automated notification flow 30 days prior to onboarding new subprocessors that will process EEA data. We cannot accept unconditional veto rights; instead: 30-day cure/fix period and alternate routing to a Dedicated EU-hosted pool if a subprocessor cannot be used.

- Retention: we can accommodate a 90-day retention for request-level logs if NovaHealth agrees to exclude debugging traces necessary to investigate incidents. Suggested clause: "Processor will purge request-level logs within 90 days unless retention is required for security incident investigation or to comply with law."

- Audit evidence: SOC 2 Type II and a summary pen-test report available under NDA. We will provide both via secure share and are open to an in-person review of controls in exceptional cases (mutually agreed scope).

I'll attach proposed redline snippets in the Security_Annex_draft.docx for ease of review.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NovaHealth DPA redlines + security annex questions

Neha —

Thanks for the quick review and the proposed middle-ground. A few follow-ups from vendor-risk and legal: 

- Audit rights: vendor-risk wants stronger language around scope (access to controls, logs related to NovaHealth data) and an ability to see evidence within 15 business days if there's a material breach. Can we shorten the breach evidence timeline?

- SOC 2: procurement needs the full SOC2 report (redacted is OK) and the date range covered. Please confirm the reporting period and if the latest report covers 2027-10 to 2028-04.

- Subprocessor effective dates: vendor-risk said they need the onboarding date and the subprocessors' geolocation. The CSV should include country of processing.

- Retention carveouts: legal says the deletion language is OK if we add an explicit exception for lawful hold.

Procurement wants to execute the DPA via AdobeSign and requested a single execution copy routed to Rachel Stone (r.stone@novahealth.com) and an ops contact (procure@novahealth.com). 

If Redwood can commit to a 15-business-day evidence window for breach-related artifacts (forensic logs), and provide SOC2 with dates, we can move the DPA to Procurement next week.

Attached: updated vendor-risk checklist (inline comments).

Best,
Amir

Amir / Rachel / Procurement —

Appreciate the clarity — quick summary and commitment items to keep momentum: 

- Evidence timing: Redwood agrees to provide breach-related artifacts necessary for NovaHealth's investigation within 15 business days of a written request in the event of a material incident. We'll add the specific wording to the Security Annex.

- SOC 2: the latest SOC 2 Type II report covers 2027-01-01 through 2027-12-31. We will upload the redacted report to a secure share once an NDA is in place; contact for the share will be marcus.lin@redwood.com.

- Subprocessor CSV: will include name, role, country(ies) of processing, and onboarding date. CSV to be uploaded by EOD tomorrow. We will also add an automated 30-day notification for new EEA-impacting subprocessors.

- Retention and lawful hold: we'll add the lawful hold carve-out language you proposed.

- Execution: AdobeSign confirmed. Please route final execution to Rachel Stone (r.stone@novahealth.com) and procure@novahealth.com. Redwood signer will be Emily Zhao (General Counsel) — we will route on AdobeSign once redlines are agreed.

Next steps / timeline: 
1) Redwood (Marcus/Neha) upload CSV + SOC2 link (NDA required) — by EOD 3/13.
2) Redwood to produce a short redline with the amended audit and retention language — by 3/14 morning.
3) Call with vendor-risk (30m) to resolve any remaining open items — propose 3/14 10am PT.
4) If call goes well, AdobeSign routing the same day to Rachel/Procurement.

If that timeline works, I will schedule the call and prepare the AdobeSign envelope ready to be sent pending final redline agreement.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
